entities.summary:
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Faqih al-Hamadani was a 10th-century Persian historian and geographer, famous for his Mukhtasar Kitab al-Buldan written in Arabic. This monumental work, comprising 100 chapters, is considered one of the earliest surviving geographic accounts of the world, covering the known world from the Indus River to the Atlantic Ocean. Al-Faqih's meticulous research and attention to detail allowed him to reconstruct the geography of the ancient world with remarkable accuracy.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Faqih al-Hamadani was a 10th-century Persian historian and geographer, famous for his Mukhtasar Kitab al-Buldan written in Arabic. This monumental work, comprising 100 chapters, is considered one of the earliest surviving geographic accounts of the world, covering the known world from the Indus River to the Atlantic Ocean. Al-Faqih's meticulous research and attention to detail allowed him to reconstruct the geography of the ancient world with remarkable accuracy.

Al-Faqih's work not only reflects his own cultural and intellectual curiosity but also had a profound impact on the development of cartography and geography in the Islamic Golden Age. His descriptions of distant lands and peoples influenced the works of later scholars, including the famous Arab geographer al-Masudi. The transmission of al-Faqih's work also played a crucial role in the spread of knowledge about the world beyond the Islamic world, contributing to the growth of a shared cultural and intellectual heritage.

The legacy of Aḥmad ibn al-Faqih can be seen in the many later works of geography and cartography that built upon his foundations. From the medieval European explorers who used his descriptions to inform their own voyages to the modern-day practitioners of geography and cartography, al-Faqih's work continues to inspire and inform our understanding of the world.
